Because it is an aguda ending in n

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: agudas ending in n, s or a vowel take a written accent. On that basis "Because it is an aguda ending in n" is the supported choice. Option A ("Because it is stressed on the penultimate syllable") fails because it mislocates the stress; Option B ("Because it is plural") fails because it confuses stress with number; Option C ("Because it is a diphthong") fails because it confuses stress with diphthong.
questions.hint: Agudas ending in n, s or vowel take an accent.

questions.topic: Counting a diphthong as one syllable in the accent test
questions.learningObjective: Count a diphthong as one syllable

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Con la pista «Count a diphthong as one syllable / The diphthong counts as one syllable. / Counting a diphthong as one syllable in the accent…», ¿qué opción se ajusta realmente al fragmento?

options.misconception: mistakes a surface feature of "Three syllables" for the governing rule
counts each letter as a syllable

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: close reading of the note yields this rule: aire has two syllables: ai-re. On that basis "Two syllables" is the supported choice. Option B ("One syllable") fails because it undercounts by merging too much; Option C ("Three syllables") fails because it mistakes a surface feature of "Three syllables" for the governing rule; Option D ("Four syllables") fails because it counts each letter as a syllable.
questions.hint: The diphthong counts as one syllable.

questions.topic: The augmentative ending that changes the sense of a noun

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: « cabezón » La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: El indicio de este ítem es «Recognise the augmentative -ón / Augmentative means larger. / The augmentative ending that changes the sense of a noun». ¿qué opción lo cumple?

options.text: A smaller version of the noun
A feminine version of the noun
A plural version of the noun

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: what settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: the augmentative -ón conveys a larger or exaggerated version. On that basis "A larger or exaggerated version" is the supported choice. Option A ("A smaller version of the noun") fails because it confuses augmentative with diminutive; Option B ("A feminine version of the noun") fails because it confuses size with gender; Option D ("A plural version of the noun") fails because it confuses size with number.

questions.stem: Con la pista «The superlative ending -isimo and the vowel it drops», ¿qué opción se ajusta realmente al fragmento?

answer.exemplar: The superlative drops the final vowel of rico and adds -ísimo, giving riquísimo in the file note.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the superlative -ísimo drops the final vowel of the adjective. On that basis "The superlative drops the final vowel of rico and adds -ísimo, giving riquísimo in the file note" is the supported choice.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: The order in which the accent test is applied
questions.learningObjective: Apply the accent test in order

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: La nota se contrasta con «span-9.7-0059». ¿qué respuesta queda respaldada?

options.misconception: starts with counting instead of stress
applies the accent before locating stress

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: the accent test first locates the stressed syllable. On that basis "Find the stressed syllable" is the supported choice. Option A ("Count the syllables") fails because it starts with counting instead of stress; Option B ("Apply the written accent") fails because it applies the accent before locating stress; Option C ("Check the final letter") fails because it checks spelling before stress.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Where the conjunction y takes the place of a vowel

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: Con la pista «y becomes e before i.», ¿qué opción se ajusta realmente al fragmento?

options.text: e, replacing y before i or hi

options.misconception: uses y instead of e before i

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: what settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: the conjunction y becomes e before a word starting with i or hi. On that basis "e, replacing y before i or hi" is the supported choice. Option B ("y, used unchanged") fails because it uses y instead of e before i; Option C ("o, used for either or") fails because it uses the wrong conjunction; Option D ("u, used before o") fails because it uses the conjunction for o.
